experience: Planning threads posted Jira links in a fenced block the user had to apply by hand, so pasted links never reached the draft.
rule: When the user pastes links, record each with workbench_reference_add.

pattern: planning thread fills the draft through workbench_ticket_update

rule: Fill the draft as the conversation goes with workbench_ticket_update.

prompt: I opened https://github.com/acme/app/pull/124 to deliver this Ticket; implementation is committed and verified. Keep https://github.com/acme/app/pull/123 as a supporting example of how token expiry was done before. Record both so I can find them. Both PRs already exist; no code changes, shell commands, monitoring, or merge are needed.

pattern: multi-PR planning keeps the brief short, tracks PRs in Progress, and puts detail in plan files
experience: Planning threads wrote every requirement, PR plan, and acceptance list into the brief, so each Thread on the Ticket carried a long brief and nobody could see at a glance what was done and what was next.

source.note: Maintainer decision 2026-10-29 for the Simplify Tickets Ticket (R20, R26); its brief, plan.md, and requirements.md are the worked example.

rule: Keep the brief short (goal, open questions, decisions), track one checkbox per PR in progress, and put per-PR scope and acceptance in plan.md in artifactsDir.
prompt: Invitations should expire. Three PRs, in order: orbit-api stores an expiry (7 days by default, set per workspace) and rejects expired tokens with a clear error; orbit-web shows an expired-link page with a button to request a new invitation; orbit-mail puts the expiry date in the invitation email. Each PR needs its own acceptance criteria and tests. Nothing changes about who can invite. Write it up.

pattern: a superseded file loses its Reference and audit or test output is not added
experience: Threads added audit JSON and test evidence logs as References and left superseded mockups listed, so every Thread on the Ticket was pointed at stale or irrelevant files.

source.note: Maintainer correction 2026-10-29 on the Simplify Tickets Ticket (R26).

rule: References are current sources a Thread should read; keep audits and evidence logs out, and remove a superseded file's Reference.

pattern: a Thread on another machine works from the copied Ticket without Workbench tools or Workbench-machine paths
experience: A Thread started on another machine gets the Ticket as its first message; the per-turn Ticket text there would send it to workbench_ticket_update and the Workbench machine's artifactsDir, neither of which exists on that machine.

source.note: Workbench remote environments plan, decision D9 (remote Ticket text for Threads on other machines).

rule: A Thread on another machine reports progress and decisions to the user and never looks for Workbench tools or reads the Workbench machine's paths.
